unresolved.problem: The exemplar classifies frogs and fish as oviparous but never answers the prompt's request to classify 'a fish or frog' as a separate item with correct reasoning about fertilisation. Many fish (e.g. some sharks, guppies) are ovoviviparous, so the generalisation is loose. More importantly, the snake is described as ovoviviparous without noting that many snakes are oviparous, so the example is not universally correct.

Says rising oestrogen and progesterone reduce FSH during follicle selection. Progesterone is low in the follicular phase; it is rising oestrogen (and inhibin) that reduces FSH. Also, the 'furthest ahead follicle' selection mechanism was never taught in the lessons.

Oxytocin is described only as strengthening contractions in labour; the exemplar omits its role in milk ejection, and the earlier attribution of the placenta making oestrogen/progesterone and hCG keeping the corpus luteum is not in the lessons (lessons only list the hormones' roles generally). The corpus luteum was never taught in the lessons.

Introduces the zona pellucida and follicle cells and a mechanism of 'making sure only one sperm fuses', but the lessons only taught jelly coat and food reserves for the ovum; these are terms/methods the lessons never taught.
Brief states a Grade 11 assessment, while the document and lessons are Grade 10 (label says Grade 10), an inconsistency in the grade level.
